title: General Liability (GL) Basics
text: GL helps cover third-party bodily injury and property damage. Typical limits are $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate. Common endorsements: Additional Insured, Primary & Non-Contributory, and Waiver of Subrogation.

title: Workers’ Compensation (WC) Basics
text: WC covers employee injuries and illnesses arising from work. It usually includes medical benefits and wage replacement. Employers Liability limits such as $1,000,000/$1,000,000/$1,000,000 are common.

title: Certificate of Insurance (COI) Basics
text: A COI shows active coverage but does not change policy terms. Typical turnaround is 1–2 business days after confirming coverage details. Requestors often ask for Additional Insured or Primary & Non-Contributory wording.

title: Waiver of Subrogation (WOS)
text: A waiver of subrogation asks the carrier to waive recovery rights against a specified party after a paid loss, when endorsed. It may increase premium and is often required by contracts.

title: Primary & Non-Contributory (PNC)
text: PNC wording seeks for your policy to respond on a primary basis and not seek contribution from the additional insured’s policy, where applicable and endorsed.

title: Umbrella / Excess Basics
text: Umbrella or excess liability can provide higher limits above GL/Auto/WC Employers Liability. Some follow form; others include exclusions. Always confirm underlying requirements.

title: Commercial Auto Symbols (BAP)
text: Symbol 1 means Any Auto. Symbol 7 means Specifically Described Autos only. Verify symbols to ensure the intended vehicles are covered.

title: Renewal Timeline (Broker Workflow)
text: T-90 gather exposures and request loss runs. T-60 market to carriers. T-30 present options and bind when possible. Communicate material changes early.

title: Claims — First Notice of Loss (FNOL)
text: Collect incident details, photos, and any witness statements. Notify the carrier or TPA promptly and preserve relevant evidence.

title: Property Coverage Basics
text: Property policies can cover buildings, contents, and business interruption. Report Total Insured Value (TIV) and update for new locations or major equipment.

title: Billing: Agency vs Direct Bill
text: Agency bill invoices come from the broker; direct bill invoices come from the carrier. Verify payee and due dates to avoid lapse.

title: Additional Insured (AI) Overview
text: Additional Insured extends certain coverage to a third party for liability arising from your operations when endorsed. Check whether it applies to ongoing and/or completed operations.
